Short answer: use <leader>snh — noice.nvim's "Noice History" — which opens the full plain-text message log in a normal buffer instead of a width-limited popup, so a long :pwd path is never truncated.
How can I see recent messages in LazyVim without the path getting cut off, like with :pwd?

codekiln's LazyVim setup runs noice.nvim and nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim with no local overrides (chezmoi/dot_config/nvim/lua/plugins/ only customizes marksman.lua, extras.lua, colorscheme.lua), so LazyVim's stock keymaps apply as shipped: <leader>snl last message, <leader>snh full history, <leader>sna all messages, <leader>snd dismiss all.
How can I see recent messages in LazyVim without the path getting cut off, like with :pwd?

<leader>n (nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Notifier "Notification History") works too for :pwd specifically, since noice routes plain msg_show messages through the same { "snacks", "notify" } backend as other notifications — its history/nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Picker view isn't clipped to the small popup's width either.
How can I see recent messages in LazyVim without the path getting cut off, like with :pwd?

<leader>snt ("Noice Picker") is listed in LazyVim's defaults but requires Telescope or fzf-lua; neither is installed here (only snacks.nvim appears in lazy-lock.json), so it won't do anything useful in this setup — <leader>snh or <leader>n are the reliable options.

How do I see more of a long filename in the nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Explorer sidebar (<leader>e)?

Short answer: the sidebar window is only 40 columns wide by default, and the Explorer picker shows filenames only (no path) with no ellipsis — long names simply get cut off at the window edge. Widen the sidebar layout in your nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim opts.
How do I see more of a long filename in the nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Explorer sidebar (<leader>e)?
Add this to the snacks.nvim plugin spec (e.g. lua/plugins/snacks.lua):
How do I see more of a long filename in the nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Explorer sidebar (<leader>e)?

This overrides only the explorer source's copy of the sidebar layout preset (width = 40 by default). To widen every picker that uses the sidebar layout preset (not just Explorer), override the preset itself instead: opts.picker.layouts.sidebar.layout.width = 60.
How do I see more of a long filename in the nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Explorer sidebar (<leader>e)?

Confirmed by reading the plugin source directly (no official width-tuning doc page): lua/snacks/picker/config/sources.lua sets M.explorer.layout = { preset = "sidebar", preview = false } and formatters.file = { filename_only = true }; lua/snacks/picker/config/layouts.lua sets M.sidebar.layout.width = 40. The filename formatter (lua/snacks/picker/format.lua, M.filename) does not truncate or ellipsize when filename_only is set — the neovim window itself clips anything past its width.

In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?

Short answer: there are two keys, and the target decides which one. gx hands the target to the operating system — the right key for an http URL, which lands in the default browser. gd follows the link inside the editor and is the better key for a link to another file in the same repository: it fires from anywhere on the link, resolves a target with no extension, and jumps to the exact heading when the link carries a #anchor.
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
gx — hand the target to the system
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
Stock nvim binds gx in normal and visual mode as a core default. LazyVim does not rebind it; it only relabels it "Open with system app" in nvim/Plugin/which-key.nvim. Answer/Official from :help gx.
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
gx — hand the target to the system
The mapping collects the target at the cursor and passes it to vim.ui.open, which shells out to open on . That is the whole story: gx never opens anything in the current editor.
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
gx — hand the target to the system

The markdown_inline treesitter highlights query tags the entire [text](destination) node with its destination, so gx fires from the label as readily as from inside the parentheses. It needs treesitter highlighting live on the buffer, which the Markdown extra provides.
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
gx — hand the target to the system

Two consequences worth knowing for a relative link: the raw path goes to open verbatim, so a .md file opens in whatever app has bound to .md rather than in the buffer; and that path is resolved against the working directory, not against the directory of the file being edited.
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
gx — hand the target to the system

A language server advertising textDocument/documentLink would take priority over the treesitter path. Marksman does not advertise it, so on a Markdown buffer here the treesitter path is always the one that runs.

Plain vim, no plugin involved: gf edits the filename under the cursor, <C-w>f opens it in a split, <C-w>gf in a new tab, and gF jumps to a line number trailing the path.

gf — follow a file path in the editor
Unlike gx, the cursor must sit on the destination inside the parentheses. On the link label, gf grabs the label word and fails.

gf — follow a file path in the editor
Resolution runs through path, which defaults to .,, — the leading . is the directory of the current file, so an ordinary relative link resolves the way the Markdown means it.

gf — follow a file path in the editor

The gaps are real: suffixesadd is empty for Markdown, so an extensionless ./file fails until it is set to .md; and a destination containing a space never resolves, with or without the <…> escape, because the filename is read through isfname, which stops at the space.

gd — follow the link with the language server
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?

The LazyVim/plugins/extras/lang/markdown extra installs the Marksman language server, and LazyVim binds gd to go-to-definition for any server advertising definition. Marksman advertises definition and references, so gd and gr both work on a Markdown buffer. Answer/Official from the Marksman README.
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
gd — follow the link with the language server

This is the strongest of the three for an in-repository link. It fires from anywhere on the link, follows ./target.md#some-heading to the heading line rather than the top of the file, resolves an extensionless ./bare to bare.md, and handles a spaced destination written either <./My Page.md> or ./My%20Page.md. A raw unescaped space is not a link at all, so nothing follows it.
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
gd — follow the link with the language server
gr lists references to the destination. <C-o> returns from the jump and <C-i> moves forward again — see vim/Keyshort/Jump/Back and Forward.
In LazyVim, how can I open a link with a keyboard shortcut?
gd — follow the link with the language server

Marksman only resolves cross-file links inside a project, meaning a Git repository or a directory holding a .marksman.toml. It finds that project by walking up from the file, not from the working directory, so a single note opened from anywhere still resolves — a garden that is neither a repository nor holds a .marksman.toml is the case that silently returns nothing. Opening from the root with nvim . is a separate habit, and what it buys is the pickers searching the whole garden.

What are , , and for symbol search, and how do they compare with ?
What are , , and for symbol search, and how do they compare with ?

Short answer: and are fuzzy-find pickers — type, filter, hit enter, the window closes. is a persistent outline sidebar that stays open while editing. is a persistent list/tree panel (closer to an IDE "Problems"/"Outline" panel) that can show symbols, diagnostics, references, and quickfix/loclist entries in one UI. All four drive "symbol search" through the same LSP textDocument/documentSymbol and workspace/symbol requests; they differ in UI paradigm, not in the underlying data source.
What are , , and for symbol search, and how do they compare with ?

(Answer/Official from nvim-telescope/telescope.nvim): a general-purpose fuzzy finder framework. Its LSP extension exposes lsp_document_symbols (current buffer) and lsp_dynamic_workspace_symbols / lsp_workspace_symbols (project-wide). Selecting a result jumps to it and the floating picker closes.
What are , , and for symbol search, and how do they compare with ?

(Answer/Official from ibhagwan/fzf-lua): the same picker concept as telescope.nvim but wraps the actual fzf binary for matching/rendering, so it's typically faster on very large result sets. It ships equivalent lsp_document_symbols and lsp_live_workspace_symbols pickers — functionally interchangeable with telescope.nvim for this use case.
What are , , and for symbol search, and how do they compare with ?

(Answer/Official from stevearc/aerial.nvim): not a fuzzy finder. It renders a live, nested tree of the current buffer's symbols (functions, classes, etc.) in a sidebar that tracks the cursor and stays open — closer to a code outline/minimap than a search box. It ships its own optional fuzzy picker for jump-to-symbol, but its primary role is the always-visible outline.
What are , , and for symbol search, and how do they compare with ?

(Answer/Official from folke/trouble.nvim): a unified list/tree panel for LSP-sourced data — diagnostics, document/workspace symbols, references, definitions, and the quickfix/location list — with folding, filtering, and persistent context while moving between items. Its "symbols" mode is the closest analogue to aerial's outline, but rendered as a togglable panel rather than an always-visible sidebar, and shared with diagnostics/references rather than outline-only.
What are , , and for symbol search, and how do they compare with ?

In this garden's actual LazyVim config: none of the telescope.nvim, fzf-lua, or aerial.nvim extras are enabled (see the My Note on LazyVim/Keyshort/Search and LazyVim/Keyshort/Code Action). General fuzzy pickers (files, grep, etc.) run on nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim instead, and document symbol search is bound to <leader>cs (Document Symbols), which opens rather than a picker or an aerial sidebar — so cheat sheets written against the telescope.nvim/fzf-lua/aerial.nvim extras (e.g. describing a <leader>ss symbol picker) don't match the keys actually bound here.
